title: Can't Wait Any Longer
description:
The next morning, {name} sits down at the goshiwon desk.

No money is coming in. Next month's rent alone is more than he has.

Another wedding announcement appears in the old high school group chat. {name} types “Congrats,” flips the phone face-down, then picks it up again and opens a job app.

Convenience store. Delivery. Café. Office temp. His thumb stops on one listing: “Mirae Industrial Tech — Office Assistant.” Four-day-a-week contract. No experience required. Excel skills preferred. Mapo-gu.

{name} opens the résumé with the six-year gap. He does not write about the family debt. The Apply button waits at the bottom of the screen.

choices.text: Send an application to Mirae Industrial Tech
choices.result_text: {name} taps Apply. The screen reads, “Application received · 9:14 a.m.”

title: 125 Years
description:
That night, back at the goshiwon.

{name} hangs his tie over the chair and opens the notebook. Beneath the first line, “five years, three billion won” is still there.

He enters the number from the interview into the phone calculator.

3 billion won ÷ 2 million won gross per month = 1,500 months
1,500 months ÷ 12 = 125 years

The number assumes he never spends a won of that pay. It is a simple division with no rent, food, taxes, or investment return built in. It is not a forecast. But the distance between the pay he has just heard and five years is clear.

A notification drops over the calculator.
[Missed Call · Father · 9:12 p.m.]

{name} looks from 125 years to Father's name and back again.

choices.text: Say it aloud: “One hundred twenty-five years.”
choices.result_text:
“One hundred twenty-five years.”

The words touch the thin wall and quickly shrink. A chair scrapes in the next room.

Beneath “five years, three billion won,” {name} writes “How.” He leaves the rest of the line blank. For now, the next four weeks are all he can fill in.

He leaves the missed-call notification where it is and opens a four-week calendar beside the notebook.

choices.text: Check the calculation once more in silence
choices.result_text:
He counts the zeroes one by one and enters the division again. The same number remains on the screen.

Beneath “five years, three billion won,” {name} writes “How.” He leaves the rest of the line blank. For now, the next four weeks are all he can fill in.

He leaves the missed-call notification where it is and opens a four-week calendar beside the notebook.

title: Mirae Industrial Tech Result
description:
In the morning, a text titled “Mirae Industrial Tech Hiring Result” arrives.

“After review, we regret that we will not be moving forward with your application.”

{name} sent the application and made it to the interview. This time, the application goes no farther.

choices.text: Close the message and record the result
choices.result_text: In the application record, {name} writes “No offer” beside Mirae Industrial Tech, then copies the interview question beneath it.

title: Seorin Trading Result
description:
A two-line email arrives from Seorin Trading's recruiting team.

“Thank you for applying. After review, we regret that we will not be moving forward with your application.”

This is the application {name} sent without hiding the employment gap. The answer is too short to hide anything at all.

choices.text: File the email in the hiring folder
choices.result_text: {name} moves the email into the hiring folder instead of deleting it. This application is over, and its status now reads “No offer.”

title: Reaching Out First
description:
Around 11 p.m. In the goshiwon's shared KakaoTalk chat, {name} finds the name of the man next door again. Kang Hyunsu. They have not messaged privately once since meeting.

{name}: "Want to study together in the kitchen for an hour tomorrow night? I'll work on my resume."

{name} presses Send. The read receipt appears, and three minutes later a reply arrives.

Hyunsu: "Sounds good, hyung. I'll bring coffee."

description_memory_if_known.relationship_memory:hyunsu:hyunsu_honest: On the night they met, {name} answered, “I don't know yet.” This time, instead of another answer, he sets aside an hour they can share.
description_memory_if_known.relationship_memory:hyunsu:hyunsu_declar: {name} said he would make it to Gangnam within five years. Instead of keeping that claim to himself, he messages Hyunsu first and asks to study together.

choices.text: Set the time for tomorrow evening
choices.result_text:
{name} checks when the shared kitchen will be free and sends a reply.

{name}: "Tomorrow at 8 p.m. See you in the kitchen."
Hyunsu: "Okay. I'll be there."

At the bottom of the chat, “Tomorrow at 8 p.m.” remains on the screen.

title: Their First Hour Together
description:
At 8 p.m. the next day, in the shared kitchen. {name} carries in his resume. Hyunsu is already there.

Two paper cups and a worn administrative-law workbook sit on the small table. {name} opens the half-revised resume across from him.

Neither leaves the table while the electric kettle boils.

choices.text: Open the resume first
choices.result_text:
{name} reads aloud the sentence explaining his employment gap. Hyunsu stops his finger on the workbook and listens to the end.

"Hyung, that last line works. It doesn't sound like an excuse."

{name} draws a line under it. Hyunsu opens his administrative-law pages again.

choices.text: Ask about Hyunsu's workbook first
choices.result_text:
"How far do you need to get tonight?"

Hyunsu opens to a folded page. "Up to here. I'll try to finish by the time you're done with your resume."

They set a one-hour timer between them. When it rings, the workbook holds new marks and the resume holds a rewritten sentence. They clear the paper cups and return to their rooms.

title: The Same Time
description:
Some time after their first study session, {name} passes through the shared kitchen on the same evening of the week. Hyunsu looks up from the table. Two paper cups sit beside his worn workbook.

"Hyung, want to study for an hour again tonight?"

He does not ask about an exam date or his chances of passing. He only asks whether they can share another hour like the first one.

{name} looks between the resume that needs another revision and the problem Hyunsu marked. Last time {name} reached out first; this time Hyunsu is the one who asks to do it again.

description_memory_if_known.relationship_memory:hyunsu:hyunsu_resume: Last time, they opened {name}'s resume first. Hyunsu still remembered the final line he had said did not sound like an excuse.
description_memory_if_known.relationship_memory:hyunsu:hyunsu_proble: Last time, they opened the page Hyunsu had folded first. {name} remembered the one-hour timer they had set and the bent corner of that page.

choices.text: "Sure. Let's do another hour."
choices.result_text:
They place a phone timer in the middle of the table. Hyunsu opens his workbook and {name} opens the resume.

When the hour ends, they agree to sit down at the same time again. Before they part, Hyunsu takes out his paper admission slip and says the exam begins at 9 a.m. on Saturday, June 27.

They make no promise that either of them will succeed. They do promise to study together again.

choices.text: "Let's start with your problem. I'll do mine after."
choices.result_text:
Hyunsu opens the folded problem, and {name} writes out the steps beside it. Forty minutes later they trade places, and Hyunsu points out an awkward sentence in the resume.

They agree to bring one thing each that has them stuck next time. Before they part, Hyunsu takes out his paper admission slip and says the exam begins at 9 a.m. on Saturday, June 27.

Work each had postponed alone becomes work someone else will see when they meet again.

title: Hanbit Distribution First Interview
description:
At 2 p.m. Thursday, in a second-floor meeting room at Hanbit Distribution's logistics center. The operations-support application {name} sent in March lies in front of the interviewer.

The interviewer places two inventory sheets side by side. One lists a system count of 184; the other lists a physical count of 179.

"The system says one hundred eighty-four, but the warehouse has only one hundred seventy-nine. What do you do first?"

There is no stock answer to recite. First he has to find out whether five units vanished, a record was late, or the first count was wrong.

choices.text: "I would reconcile the receiving and shipping records in chronological order."
choices.result_text:
"I would start from the last point when the numbers matched. Then I would compare the receiving slips, shipping slips, and return records in order."

The interviewer asks, "And if none of the records explain it?"

"I would report it as an unresolved discrepancy instead of changing the count to make it match."

The interviewer writes down the answer and turns the page. It is not time to give a result yet.

choices.text: "I would recount with the floor lead and find when the discrepancy began."
choices.result_text:
"Before changing anything in the system, I would recount the same items with the floor lead. We would also check whether anything was moved or staged for shipping."

The interviewer asks, "What if those items have to ship today?"

"I would report the confirmed quantity separately from the quantity still under review. I would not treat the missing five as if they were there."

The interviewer gives a short nod and reads the next question. It is not time to give a result yet.

title: This Time, First
description:
Not long after the night shift begins, {name} opens the door of the same convenience store.

He does need a few things, but they are not the only reason he came at this hour.

Kim Daeun looks up from the price tags she is sorting behind the counter. She studies his face for a moment, then asks first.

"{name}, right?"

choices.text: "Daeun. Another night shift?"
choices.result_text:
"You remembered my name. Yes, I'm here until dawn again."

Daeun sets down the price tags in her hand. {name} asks whether working this late is hard, and she says it is manageable once the busiest hour passes.

choices.text: "I enjoyed the extra gimbap last time. Thanks again."
choices.result_text:
"It was two-for-one. I was just letting you know."

Daeun smiles. "Still, I'm glad you enjoyed it."

{name} thanks her once more and finishes paying. As he opens the door to leave, Daeun says, "Check the sale tags first next time, {name}."

{name} laughs. "I will, Daeun."

title: The Greeting Left Unsaid
description:
The convenience store where a clerk pointed out the two-for-one deal that dawn. Last time, {name} left after saying only thank you.

When he sets a triangle kimbap on the counter, the clerk studies his face.

"You were here last time, right? You took the extra one from the two-for-one."

They remember each other's faces. They still do not know each other's names.

choices.text: "Last time, all I said was thanks. I'm {name}."
choices.result_text:
The clerk looks briefly surprised, then bows in greeting.

"I'm Kim Daeun. I work the night shift."

"Daeun."
"And you're {name}."

choices.text: "Thanks for pointing out the two-for-one last time."
choices.result_text:
"You remembered. It really wasn't much."

The clerk asks as she hands him the receipt, "What's your name, by the way?"

{name} introduces himself first, and she answers, "I'm Kim Daeun."

title: Looking for a Room
description:
Early April, on a Sinchon side street after the spring rain. {name} opens the door of a small real-estate office to find out whether he can leave the goshiwon.

The man across the desk places a basement studio listing beside the calculator.

"Ten million won deposit, five hundred fifty thousand a month. Maintenance is separate."

Even the deposit is far beyond what {name} has. As he taps the calculator a few more times, the man quietly watches his fingers, then his worn sneakers.

"That would be difficult in your situation."

{name} pushes back his chair to stand. The man takes out two paper cups.

"Wait. You can't rent this place, but that doesn't mean I have to send you straight back out. I can still make you a warm cup of coffee."

choices.text: "How did you know about my situation?"
choices.result_text:
The man sets down the papers in his hand and looks at {name}.

"Was I wrong?"

{name} does not answer. The man motions toward the empty chair with his chin. His gaze now feels less like kindness than verification.

choices.text: "I'll have the coffee, then leave."
choices.result_text:
The paper cup is hot enough to warm his hands, and the instant coffee is too sweet.

When {name} sits again, the man moves a file aside, revealing the desk plaque beneath it: “Licensed Real-Estate Agent Im Sangchul.”

{name} still does not know why he is spending time on someone who cannot afford the room.

title: A Message After Ten Years
description:
Late at night. A familiar name appears in KakaoTalk: Choi Jaehyuk.

"Hey, {name}. It's Jaehyuk—Choi Jaehyuk. We served together. Remember me? Been a while. How've you been?"

They were twenty-two and in the same barracks. After discharge they checked in a few times, then a changed number ended the contact.

{name} opens the reply field. It is his turn to cross ten years in one sentence.

choices.text: "Of course I remember. It's been a long time."
choices.result_text:
{name}: "Of course I remember. How've you been?"

Jaehyuk: "I've been all right. My number changed, so I only just found you again."

They briefly trade the names of people they knew in the army and the neighborhoods where they live now. They do not set a date to meet. The conversation that had gone quiet rises to the top of the KakaoTalk list again.

choices.text: "Yeah, I remember. What's this about all of a sudden?"
choices.result_text:
{name}: "Yeah, I remember. What's this about all of a sudden?"

Jaehyuk: "Nothing happened. You just crossed my mind after all this time, so I reached out. Sorry if that bothered you."

{name}: "No. It just caught me off guard."

After a few more lines of small talk, the chat stops. They have not made plans to meet yet.

title: An Offer from Hanbit Distribution
description:
On Tuesday morning, a text arrives from Hanbit Distribution's recruiting team.

“Following your first interview, we would like to offer you a contract position in logistics-center operations support. Please let us know by 6:00 p.m. today whether you can start Monday.”

{name} remembers the application he sent in March and the inventory sheets on the conference-room table in April. The interview result has returned as a single question: Will he show up for work?

choices.text: "I can start Monday."
choices.result_text:
{name} replies that he can start. A moment later, another message arrives with his start time and a list of things to bring.

His first paycheck covers the three weeks from Monday's start through month-end: 1.68 million won. Full months after that pay 2.24 million won. What remains is reaching Hanbit Distribution's logistics center on time Monday morning.

choices.text: "Thank you for the offer, but I have to decline."
choices.result_text:
{name} adds a brief explanation and sends the reply.

“Understood. Thank you for applying.”

That closes the hiring process. His application record now holds the interview, the offer, and his decision not to take it.

title: Next Tuesday
description:
On {name}'s third visit to the convenience store, the counter is quiet. Daeun changes the receipt roll, then asks him a question.

"{name}, did you eat dinner today?"

When he answers, she nods. Last time she remembered his name. This time she remembers to ask whether he ate this late at night.

"I'm always the one asking first, aren't I? Next time, ask how I'm doing too."

choices.text: "Then I'll come back at this time next Tuesday."
choices.result_text:
Daeun checks the clock on the wall and smiles.

"I'll be here at this time Tuesday. Even if we can't talk long, let's at least ask each other how the day went."

When {name} nods, Daeun looks up at the clock once more.

choices.text: "All right. But you can't skip your late meal either."
choices.result_text:
Daeun laughs and holds up one finger.

"Then next time, we start with, 'Did you eat?' No fair if only one of us gets to nag."

{name} holds up one finger too.

title: One More Question
description:
On {name}'s third visit to the convenience store, Daeun is putting price tags on a new delivery.

"Welcome."

Even after learning each other's names, they have exchanged little more than brief greetings across the counter. {name} finishes paying but does not walk straight to the door. This time, he is the one who adds something more.

choices.text: "Daeun, was it any less busy tonight?"
choices.result_text:
Daeun sets down the bundle of price tags.

"It was hectic until a few minutes ago, but I can breathe now. What about you?"

{name} answers with two sentences about his day. When a customer comes in, Daeun picks up the bundle of price tags and returns to the register.

choices.text: "Last time I only told you my name. Most days, I don't get done until around this time."
choices.result_text:
Daeun listens without leaning across the counter.

"So that's why you always come in around this time. By the time my shift ends, the whole day is gone too."

{name} says that next time, he will ask about her day.

title: The Main Road Again
description:
A few weeks later, after the rain, {name} walks the same neighborhood road he took home from the bus stop. Han Jiyeon stands beside her black sedan at the wet curb.

"We barely got to say a proper hello last time."

Jiyeon points to a cafe across the street.

"If you have time, let's grab a coffee. I won't bring up compensation. I came because I wanted the chance to actually talk this time."

The light changes, and people pass between them.

choices.text: "Sure—somewhere nearby."
choices.result_text:
They enter a small cafe across the street. Jiyeon does not return to the accident.

Instead, she asks which roads {name} takes most often in this neighborhood and which place in Seoul he learned first. {name} asks whether she comes to this area often.

With half the coffee still left, Jiyeon asks her next question.

choices.text: "If this isn't about compensation, we can talk while we walk."
choices.result_text:
Jiyeon glances at the cafe, then nods. They walk one block along the main road.

{name} asks why she came back to this neighborhood. She says their last conversation was so short that it stayed on her mind. Then she asks what he has been doing lately.

choices.text: "I think I'll just leave."
choices.result_text:
{name} bows his head in farewell and walks toward the crosswalk.

Jiyeon does not follow or call after him. A car door closes behind him.

title: A Second Cup of Instant Coffee
description:
{name} takes Im Sangchul's business card from his wallet, calls the number on it, and asks if he can stop by again.

A few days later, in the same real-estate office, Sangchul serves instant coffee in the same paper cups.

"You came back. So if it isn't a room this time, what are you looking for?"

{name} admits that he still does not know where to begin. Instead of answering, Sangchul places a blank sheet of paper and a pen in the middle of the desk.

choices.text: "I want to learn at my own pace instead of rushing."
choices.result_text:
Sangchul takes a sip from his paper cup and nods.

"That doesn't mean you're slow. It means you aren't running on someone else's timetable."

{name} folds the blank sheet and slips it into his pocket.

choices.text: "I'll start by recording where my own money goes."
choices.result_text:
{name} writes rent, food, and transportation at the top of the page. Sangchul does not supply any numbers. He only asks whether anything is missing.

When {name} leaves the office, the page holds several expenses to check before the month ends.

title: Together at a Pojangmacha Again
description:
After a few more KakaoTalk messages, they agree to meet at a pojangmacha on Saturday evening.

Jaehyuk dresses more sharply than he did in the army, but his laugh sounds the same. As soon as they sit down, they remember a night spent on guard duty together and the time they nearly missed the bus back from leave.

"Ten years, and I still remember this stuff."

Until the last skewer is gone, Jaehyuk asks where {name} lives now, and {name} asks where he has been. Out of a decade apart, the nights they both remember return first.

choices.text: "Let's take a photo so we don't lose track of each other again."
choices.result_text:
Jaehyuk props up his phone and starts the timer. Under the tent lights, they lean shoulder to shoulder and smile.

A moment later, the photo arrives on {name}'s phone. For the first time, the two of them are in the same frame without their uniforms.

"Next time, let's not wait so long."

Neither of them laughs the words away.

choices.text: Keep the night to old stories and leave first
choices.result_text:
{name} checks the time of the last train and sets down his glass.

"Let's call it a night. It was good to see you again."

Jaehyuk does not press him to stay. He smiles and offers his hand. They talk at length about the army, but only as much as they need to about their present lives.

The warmth of seeing him remains. The distance between them can close more slowly.

title: The Pharmacy Bag
description:
On Monday morning, June 1, a message arrives from Mr. Choi, Father's neighbor in Changwon.

“Minjun, I've seen your father come home with a pharmacy bag a few times lately. It looks like he's been going to a hospital, but I couldn't ask what was wrong. Give him a call.”

{name} calls Father immediately. The phone rings for a long time, but he does not answer. Eleven minutes later, a short text arrives from Father.

“I'm fine. Don't worry about it.”

description_memory_if_known.relationship_memory:father:father_gangna: On that call, he had stopped short of saying anything about Gangnam. Today, the unsaid words remain between a short text and the long stretch of ringing.
description_memory_if_known.relationship_memory:father:father_quiet_: On that call, he had let Father's “Yeah” be the last word and ended the call himself. Today, he keeps the phone to his ear until the ringing stops.
description_memory_if_known.relationship_memory:father:father_asked_: On that call, one more question had brought a brief laugh from the other end. Today, the same number gives him only a long stretch of ringing.

choices.text: Ask Mr. Choi which hospital it was
choices.result_text:
{name}: “Did you happen to see which hospital it was?”

Mr. Choi replies that he does not know the name. Over the past ten days, he twice saw Father return from the nearby bus stop carrying a pharmacy bag. {name} writes two dates and “pharmacy bag” in his notebook.

choices.text: Try calling again tonight
choices.result_text: That evening, {name} calls Father again. He waits until the ringing stops, but Father still does not answer. He writes down the morning text and the time of this second attempt.

choices.text: Close the message and check this month's calendar
choices.result_text: {name} closes the message and opens the calendar. Empty spaces and existing commitments share the same screen. The space for another call to Father is still blank.

title: Dodam Customer Center Result
description:
One morning in the second week of June, a text arrives from Dodam Customer Center's recruiting team.

“Thank you for applying. After review, we will not be moving forward with your customer-operations application.”

The receipt number from the April application remains at the bottom of the message. The message contains no interview date.

choices.text: Check the receipt number and result
choices.result_text:
{name} confirms that the receipt number in the text matches the one received in April.

This hiring process ends here. There is no interview date and no further message to answer.

title: City Facilities Work-Sample Request
description:
On Wednesday afternoon, June 17, a text arrives from City Facilities Operations.

“To support our application review, please submit a sample facilities-inspection worksheet. The deadline is 6:00 p.m. on Friday, June 26.”

The attachment includes a fictional inspection scenario and a blank form: “Civic gym, basement level one; two emergency lights not working; site recheck required.” The task is to organize it by date, facility, issue status, and action. It is neither an interview notice nor an offer.

choices.text: Confirm the deadline and attachment
choices.result_text:
{name} checks “6:00 p.m. on Friday, June 26” and the attachment's filename again in the text.

The cursor blinks in the worksheet's first row.

title: City Facilities Hiring Result
description:
At 11:06 on a Monday morning in late July, several weeks after the work sample was sent, a text arrives from City Facilities Operations.

“We reviewed your facilities-inspection worksheet, but we will not be proceeding to an interview for this contract position.”

It carries the same application number as the receipt text from June 26. No interview has been scheduled.

choices.text: Check the application number and result
choices.result_text:
{name} confirms that both texts carry the same application number.

Submitting the worksheet on time was everything he could still do for this application. This hiring process ends here.

title: The Tuesday They Promised
description:
Around 1 a.m. on Tuesday, June 2, at the time they agreed on while looking at the wall clock, {name} opens the convenience-store door.

Daeun looks up from the stock she is sorting behind the counter.

“You really came. We said we'd ask each other how yesterday went, remember?”

choices.text: "How was yesterday, Daeun?"
choices.result_text:
Daeun thinks for a moment, then says yesterday's delivery was larger than usual. {name} answers honestly with one task he finished yesterday and one he put off.

When a customer enters, Daeun returns to the register and {name} steps aside toward the shelves.

choices.text: "I'll start with yesterday—one thing I finished and one I put off."
choices.result_text: {name} names one thing he finished yesterday and one he put off. Daeun answers with the busiest part of yesterday's shift and the moment she finally caught her breath.

title: One Last Problem Before the Exam
description:
Around 10 p.m. on Sunday, June 21, a Kakao message arrives from Hyunsu.

Hyunsu: “Hyung, the exam starts at nine next Saturday morning, and there's one question I still can't get straight. Do you have a minute?”

A photo of an administrative-law question follows. Hyunsu waits for an answer after sending it. {name} enlarges the image.

choices.text: Review only this one problem together
choices.result_text:
Instead of calling, {name} points out the numbered sentences in the photo by message. Hyunsu finds the one condition missing from his own work.

{name}: “Let's stop here. Don't open anything else.”
Hyunsu: “Okay. I'll sort this one out and go to bed.”

They stop after one problem.

choices.text: Tell him to close it and sleep now
choices.result_text:
{name}: “Starting something new now might make it worse. Mark it and get some sleep.”

Hyunsu replies a moment later.

“Okay. I'll set my alarm and go to bed. You should get some sleep too, hyung.”

The conversation ends there.

title: The Morning the Exam Began
description:
A little after 9 a.m. on Saturday, June 27, the exam Hyunsu mentioned is already under way.

{name} opens Kakao, but there is no new message beneath their last conversation. There is nothing to do but wait until the exam ends.

choices.text: Send nothing until the exam is over

title: An Initial Verification Call
description:
On Wednesday morning, June 24, an unknown number calls.

“This is the police cybercrime unit. We need to ask a few preliminary questions about an account in your name. Today, we'll only confirm a few facts and ask which dates you're available to come in.”

In late February, {name} returned 1.5 million won of the 2 million won he had received after the bank issued a victim-funds return request. He closed the account and blocked the recruiter. The remaining 500,000 won is still part of the facts.

This call does not yet state a charge or disposition.

choices.text: Give only the facts in the order you remember them
choices.result_text:
{name} gives the dates in order: when the account was handed over, when the money arrived, when the bank sent the return request, and when he agreed to return 1.5 million won.

The investigator reads back the dates and asks which weekdays he is available to come in. The call ends without a conclusion.

choices.text: Ask for the case number and a written list of requested materials
choices.result_text:
{name} writes down the department and case number and asks for the requested materials by text or in writing.

The investigator agrees to send a confirmation and asks which dates he is available to come in. No lawyer or disposition is discussed.

title: Another Text from the Recruiter
description:
On Wednesday morning, June 24, a text arrives from a new number.

“Three more, same as last time. You can do it, right? Answer today.”

There is no sender name. After {name} handed over three bankbooks and debit cards in late February, names and account numbers in the same format have returned to the screen.

This message gives neither a payment amount nor a location.

choices.text: Do not answer; block the number
choices.result_text:
{name} sends no reply and blocks the number.

Only one text has been stopped. The three sets handed over before, and whatever followed them, have not disappeared.

choices.text: Capture the screen and preserve it with the date
choices.result_text:
{name} takes a screenshot with the sender and time visible and leaves the original message intact.

The sender and time of today's message remain in the record.

title: An Evening Walk at Gangnam Station
description:
Commuters pour out of Gangnam Station in the evening. {name} stops outside a cafe window.

An Americano on the menu costs 9,000 won. The banking app shows the current balance and the fixed costs due at the end of this month separately.

What {name} can decide now is whether to spend that 9,000 won or leave it for those bills.

choices.text: Buy the 9,000-won coffee and keep the receipt
choices.result_text:
{name} pays 9,000 won for an Americano. The paper receipt shows the amount and time of payment.

He sits by the window for ten minutes, then leaves. The evening in Gangnam now has a price: 9,000 won, printed on a single receipt.

choices.text: Check the price and leave without ordering
choices.result_text:
{name} looks once more at the 9,000-won price and turns away from the counter.

No new charge appears in the banking app, and the 9,000-won price remains behind him at the counter.

choices.text: Check this month's fixed costs before buying coffee
choices.result_text:
{name} steps away from the counter and opens the banking app again. He subtracts the fixed costs due at the end of this month from the current balance.

No coffee charge appears. He confirms how much has to stay in the account to make it through the month.

title: The First Dawn Behind the Counter
description:
After 4 a.m., the customers stop coming. {name} restacks the parcel boxes by size and runs a mop over the sticky floor. Only the hum of the refrigerators and buzz of the fluorescent lights remain behind the counter.

His hand stops at an empty slot on the shelf beneath the cigarette chart. {name} finds the same brand in the stockroom and fills the gap.

choices.text: Write the finishing time on the shift sheet
choices.result_text:
{name} takes a pen from the apron pocket and fills in the final box on the shift sheet. Cardboard dust and detergent linger together on his fingertips.

As he leaves, the morning delivery truck stops outside. The one-day cover shift is over, and the pay for the hours worked is in his account.

title: The Fourth Night of Barcodes
description:
The wall clock is already past handoff time. In front of the last shelf, {name} lowers the scanner and flexes his stiff wrist once.

The cart he pushed along the same aisle for four nights rests at an angle by his feet.

description_memory_if_known.activity_task_outcome:m3_inventory_shift: A second count still finds eleven items on the shelf. The receiving and returns logs also show that an item moved to the returns holding area the previous night remains in the system count. He found the cause, but his wrist aches and the handoff note lies blank beneath the fluorescent light.

A second count still finds eleven items on the shelf. The handoff note records the system's twelve, the shelf's eleven, and the check time. Even after setting the handoff sheet down, the blank line for the cause remains in {name}'s mind.

The receiving and returns logs show that one item moved to the returns holding area the previous night. The handoff note records that entry and the difference between the system's twelve and the shelf's eleven. Because he never recounts the shelf, {name} cannot shake the thought that eleven itself might be wrong.

A second count still finds eleven items on the shelf. The records show that one item moved to the returns holding area the previous night remains in the system count. The handoff note includes the difference, check time, and cause. By the time all three tasks are done, handoff time is long past. Only then does {name} feel his wrist and lower back stiffen at once.
A second count still finds eleven items on the shelf. {name} marks the check time and shelf number beside the discrepancy.

choices.text: Check the payment and leave the warehouse
choices.result_text:
{name} returns the cart and lights up his phone. The 360,000-won inventory-count payment is in his account.

The lights of the first bus pass through the gap beneath the warehouse shutter. Four nights of scanner beeps have stopped. Only the fluorescent hum remains in the warehouse before dawn.

title: The Row That Doesn't Balance
description:
From a seat at the back of the youth-center classroom, {name} watches the instructor project a sheet of receiving, shipping, and returns and ask the class to find the row that does not balance.

{name} copies the inventory-turnover formula into his notebook three times. The first two use the wrong denominator. Only the third matches the sample sheet.

description_memory_if_known.activity_task_outcome:m3_inventory_shift: As {name} starts to write beside the mismatched row, he remembers the handoff note he left blank last month even after finding the cause.

When he looks back up at the mismatched row, {name} remembers the night he confirmed eleven items and wrote down the difference but never found the entry that caused it. He works through the rows before and after the mismatch one by one.
His hand pauses over the figures. He remembers the eleven items on the shelf he never went back to recount last month.
As the instructor works through each check, {name} remembers the night he stayed with all three tasks past handoff time.
As {name} follows the mismatched row, he remembers the check time and shelf number he wrote beside the discrepancy last month.

choices.text: Leave the two wrong lines on the page
choices.result_text:
{name} strikes through the two wrong formulas and writes one sentence beside each explaining the mistake. When class ends, the instructor closes the attendance sheet.

His notebook holds one place to start the next time he faces a stock sheet.

title: Outside the Fourth Home
description:
On the fourth evening, outside the last home, six boxes and a stack of folded moving blankets still stand between the entrance and the truck. {name} wraps the tape around his palm again and pushes the empty dolly toward the door.

While he straightens his back, another worker silently rolls one wrist. No one calls for a break. They simply take opposite sides of the next box.

choices.text: Check the bottom of the box before lifting
choices.result_text:
After feeling for damp cardboard underneath, they lift the first box on the same beat. They move the remaining five the same way, then secure the last box between the moving blankets.

When the cargo door shuts, the metal noise that has followed them for four days stops. The job is over, but his palms and lower back still feel heavy.

title: The Sunday Left Empty
description:
The room is already bright when {name} opens his eyes. He reaches for the phone to check the time, then pulls his hand away from where it lies face down. Doors open and close a few times in the hall before the building goes quiet again.

He fills a washed cup with water and reheats a meal. He does not read any job postings, and the waiting messages go unanswered.

choices.text: Make no plans until the light fades
choices.result_text:
{name} sleeps once more and wakes near evening. Relief at having rested arrives alongside the emptiness of letting a day pass.

He picks up the phone and lights the screen but makes no new plans. Sunday fades that way, and Monday is still coming.

title: The First Bill

description_memory_if_known.relationship_memory:father:father_neighb: The notebook still holds the two dates confirmed with Mr. Choi and the words “pharmacy bag.”
description_memory_if_known.relationship_memory:father:father_called: The notebook holds the morning text and, on the next line, the time he called again that evening.
description_memory_if_known.relationship_memory:father:father_health: The space left for a call to Father on the June 1 calendar is still blank.

choices.text: Read Father's last message again
choices.result_text:
{name} opens the short message from Father.

“I'm fine. Don't worry about it.”

There is no diagnosis and no hospital name. The call button sits directly below the message.

choices.text: Subtract this month's fixed costs from the balance
choices.result_text:
{name} subtracts each fixed cost from the balance and copies the amount on the screen onto the first line of the notebook.

{v2_first_bill_after_bills}

choices.text: Check his wrists and back
choices.result_text:
{name} slowly opens and closes his hands, then lifts his back away from the chair.

He checks his wrists and back for strain. Whatever he chooses tonight, they will have to bear it.

title: The First Bill
description:
{name} writes down only the things he can still do now.

{v2_first_bill_tradeoffs}

Once a deadline passes, that task can no longer be completed tonight. Finishing any of the other tasks involving people, money, or rest will also leave no time for the others. He cannot start everything and finish nothing. He has to choose one task and complete it.

{name} decides which line to circle.

choices.text: Call Father again
choices.result_text:
{name} calls Father. After several rings, his father answers.

“Yeah?”
“I just wanted to hear your voice. Have you eaten?”
“I did. Take care of yourself.”

When {name} brings up the hospital, Father asks whether the room is cold. Neither answers the question the other one asked. Long silences pass between talk of dinner, the weather, and buses to Changwon.

{name}: “I'll call again Monday evening.”
Father: “If you want.”

After the call, {name} writes “Father” in Monday's space in the notebook.

choices.text: Finish Hanbit Distribution's month-end discrepancy sheet
choices.result_text:
{name} reopens the month-end discrepancy sheet from the logistics center. Of the two rows where system and physical counts disagree, he corrects only the one he can trace. Beside the other, he writes “site recheck” instead of inventing a quantity.

At 5:59 p.m., he sends the first month-end sheet assigned to him since joining Hanbit. Fifteen minutes later, the person in charge asks why one field is blank. {name} separates what the records prove from what still needs checking.

After seven, a reply comes back: update it Monday after the site count. The other row on the sheet still reads “site recheck.”

choices.text: Submit the City Facilities worksheet
choices.result_text:
{name} reopens the worksheet he drafted. His hand stops over whether to mark the broken emergency lights “resolved” or “site recheck required.” He does not invent a completion time absent from the scenario. He records only the date, facility, issue, and next action.

At 5:59 p.m., he sends the file. The automated reply contains only “Work sample received” and an application number. {name} opens the submitted copy once more, checks every blank against its source, and transfers the number to his notebook.

choices.text: Go to Daeun's store and ask whether she ate
choices.result_text:
{name} leaves his room at once. After changing subway lines, he reaches the store during the night shift he learned about before.

{name}: “My turn to ask first. Daeun, did you eat?”
Daeun: “I had a gimbap before my shift. What about you?”

Before {name} can say not yet, a customer walks in. Once the sale and a parcel drop-off are done, Daeun nods toward the triangle-gimbap shelf.

Daeun: “If you came to make sure I ate, get something for yourself too.”
{name}: “Then I'll believe you ate.”
Daeun: “Only halfway. I only ate half.”

{name} buys one and eats at the window where he can still see the counter. Their conversation stops whenever another customer enters, then starts again. When he checks the last-train schedule and stands to leave, Daeun waves from behind the register.

choices.text: Message Jaehyuk first and ask about his week
choices.result_text:
{name}: “I'm done for today. How was your week?”

Jaehyuk says he is still out. At first, all he sends is, “Same as always.” When {name} goes first with one thing he finished and one thing he postponed, Jaehyuk writes a long message about something he got wrong on the way home.

The replies stop and start between subway transfers and dinner. {name} types an easy joke, deletes it, and names what he postponed without dressing it up. Investment and money never come up.

After ten, Jaehyuk writes.

“Next time, let's each say one thing we did right too.”

choices.text: Reconcile this month's expense ledger at home
choices.result_text:
{name} spreads receipts across the desk where he lives now. He lists rent, food, transit, and phone payments by date. The first total does not match the card history, so he works down every line again.

The missing entries are two meals paid in cash and a transit-card top-up. Instead of filling the amounts from memory, he finds the receipts and the reload record and places each beside its date. Only on the third calculation does the notebook match the amount that left the account.

After nine, he draws two lines beneath the total on the first page. Sangchul's business card stays in the drawer.

choices.text: Take urgent paid work tonight
choices.result_text:
{name} leaves the room at once to reach the 6:30 p.m. assembly. The foreman of the overnight loading crew checks his gloves and work zone before asking his name. His palms start rubbing raw inside the gloves before the first pallet is empty.

After midnight, straightening his back takes one extra beat as he unloads the last box. The foreman checks the account number on {name}'s phone. A moment later, the 280,000-won day rate arrives.

The deposit alert glows beneath the reflection of his raw, reddened palm.

choices.text: Set one alarm and lie down first
choices.result_text:
Before 6:00 p.m., {name} sets one alarm and puts the phone face down. He showers in lukewarm water, slowly drinks a glass of water, and leaves only the notebook and pen beside the bed.

Even after lying down, the order of everything he should do rearranges itself in his head. Each time his hand moves to check, it stops at the face-down phone. He starts nothing new while doors and footsteps in the hall grow distant.

title: The First Bill

description_memory_if_known.m3_ledger_reasons_named: The March ledger had reasons beside its entries. The line he circled tonight could not be reduced to one figure either.
description_memory_if_known.m3_ledger_totals_only: In March, he had stopped at the total. Tonight, what he finished and what he put off could not be folded into one number.

choices.text: Read the page once and close the notebook
choices.result_text:
{name} checks the next actions written on the previous page once more. On a new page, he writes only “Monday, June 29” and leaves the rest blank.

He closes the notebook and sets the pen on top.

title: The Ledger in the Room
description:
One evening in March, {name} starts the laundry and returns to his room. He lays the receipts out by date on the floor between the bed and the desk.

Rent, meals, transit. He checks each receipt against the payment history on his phone. Two convenience-store receipts show nearly the same amount, but one is from early morning and the other from late at night. The figures look alike; the parts of his life that required them do not.

After two passes, the total balances. The sum is right, but nothing on the page says which line belonged to which kind of day.

The laundry alarm sounds. Before going to empty the machine, {name} rests the tip of his pen in the first blank space beside an entry. He has to decide whether this month will keep only the figures, or why he spent the money behind them.

choices.text: Add a reason beside each entry
choices.result_text:
{name} keeps the notes short: “Finished late.” “Skipped a meal.” “Needed to make it through the next day.” Once the reasons are there, similar amounts divide into money he can cut and money whose absence would make the day collapse first.

By the time he returns with the laundry, the ink is dry. The reasons take up more room on the page than the total.

choices.text: Reconcile the totals first
choices.result_text:
{name} checks every amount once more and draws a double line beneath the total. What he needs tonight is not an interpretation, but a figure that is not wrong. He leaves the reason column blank.

After folding the laundry away, he closes the notebook. The page is orderly, and the reason column stays blank to the end.

title: What Matters in a Room
description:
One afternoon in April, the queue display at the housing-welfare desk in a community center flashes a new number. Carrying an envelope of receipts and his notebook, {name} sits down across from the counselor.

She turns an A4 sheet sideways and, across the top, writes down the deposit, monthly rent, maintenance fee, brokerage fee, and moving cost. At the end she adds, “Cash available after the move.”

“If we start with listings, rent and deposit will take over the page. Let's start with what you'll still need after the move.”

Below those figures, she divides the page into three boxes: “Cash available after the move.” “A space where I can close the door and be alone.” “Round-trip time to the places I go often.” He does not yet know whether one room can meet all three standards. Today is not about choosing a room. It is about choosing the first standard he will not discard while looking.

Her pen stops above the page. She points to each box in turn. “If you protect one of these first, which one will it be?”

choices.text: Keep enough cash to last after the move
choices.result_text:
“I want enough left to last for a while after I move.”

The counselor underlines the final column in the calculation across the top. “Then, for every listing, calculate how much cash you could still use after setting aside the deposit and paying the moving costs. Being able to move in is not the same as being able to stay.”

When the consultation ends, {name} folds the sheet so that “Cash available after the move” faces outward. His number disappears from the display, but those words remain on the first line of his notebook.

choices.text: Find a room where I can close the door and have the space to myself
choices.result_text:
“A room where I can come back, close the door, and have the space to myself.”

The counselor circles “A space where I can close the door and be alone.” “Then look at the door and the walls before the floor area. Check which spaces you would still have to share.”

Beside it, {name} writes, “Where does the noise stop?” He now has one question to ask before he asks how large a room is.

choices.text: Spend less of the day in transit
choices.result_text:
“I want to spend less time traveling to the places I go often.”

The counselor places the rent column beside the round-trip column. “Then write a month of travel time next to the difference in rent. A room that looks cheaper can still take more of each day.”

Outside, while waiting through a single crosswalk signal, the word “round trip” in his notebook already looks like a line of figures.
